signIn.noWallet: You don't need a wallet or a balance: Solvers takes care of that.
signIn.p1: Sign in with your email. We send you an access code and create your account on the spot.
signIn.p2: Publishing is free, with no deposit and no monthly fee.
signIn.p3: Every version goes through an automated check and a review by our team before it goes live.

build.toolSub: A free solver, included in the platform
build.toolText: It walks you through seven steps: the promise and the audience, what sets it apart, the process, the knowledge, the tools, the first conversation and the test cases. At the end it hands you the finished package, already checked by the same validator the site uses.
build.installNote: Installing takes about two minutes and works with Claude and ChatGPT. After that, just ask: “Use Solver Builder to build a solver about [your topic]”.
build.zipTitle: What the ZIP should look like
build.zipTree:
my-solver.zip
├─ manifest.json
├─ steps/       (3 to 6 steps, .md)
├─ knowledge/   (knowledge, .md)
├─ templates/   (ready-made templates)
└─ evals/cases/ (test cases, .json)
build.zipNote: manifest.json goes at the root, not inside an extra folder. Up to {size}.
build.noZipTitle: If your AI can't generate the ZIP
build.noZipText: Some AIs only show the files in the chat. In that case, Solver Builder hands you each file in its own block, with step-by-step instructions to save each one in a folder and compress it. The site checks everything again when you upload.
build.guide: Complete format guide, inside Solver Builder
build.haveZip: I have the ZIP, upload it
build.locked: Uploading opens once your registration and contact are complete

track.text: After you upload, each package goes through these stages. You can follow everything in My submissions and you'll be notified when our team replies.

summary.title: Summary of what you accept
summary.b1: You are responsible for the package's content and have the right to use everything in it. Third-party content needs a source and permission.
summary.b2: Our team reviews every version before it goes live and may ask for changes, reject, suspend or remove a solver.
summary.b3: The platform fee comes out of each sale. The rest goes to your wallet.
summary.b4: A solver may not promise financial, legal or medical results without caveats, act against the user, or send their data elsewhere.

profile.terms: I've read the summary and accept the Solvers terms for creators.

contact.title: Contact for notices and help requests
contact.okText: All set: we'll notify you there when our team replies to a submission or when a buyer asks for help.
contact.text: Before you submit a solver, link your Telegram. That's how we notify you about submissions and how buyers ask for help, without seeing your contact. Click Link Telegram: the site generates a code and you send it to the Solvers bot.
contact.saveFirst: Save your registration first (name, introduction and terms): the button to link appears right after.
contact.later: You can save your registration now and link later, but uploading a package only opens once your contact is linked.

errors.sessionExpired: Your session expired. Sign in again and try once more.

own.title: The license is yours.
own.text: The permanent license is recorded on the Solana network, in your wallet.

resell.title: Resell what you don't use.
resell.text: Finished the project? List the license and get part of the price back.

creator.title: The creator earns on every resale on Solvers.
creator.text: A share of each sale made through the marketplace goes to whoever created the solver.

list.title: List the license
list.text: In your library, pick the permanent license you no longer use and set the price.

buy.title: Someone buys it
buy.text: The buyer pays and the license moves to their wallet right away, and you lose access. The solver's rating stays with it; personal reviews stay with whoever wrote them.

paid.title: Everyone gets paid
paid.text: Through the Solvers marketplace, you receive the sale price and the creator receives the royalty, automatically.

resale.title: Resell the license you no longer use
resale.lead: The permanent license is yours. When the resale marketplace opens, you'll be able to sell the license for a solver you no longer use, and the creator earns a share of every resale made through Solvers.
resale.meanwhileText: Your permanent licenses are already recorded in your wallet. When resale opens, the option to list appears in your library, next to each license.

cloak.title: Withdraw privately
cloak.gateText: Use the same account as your creator dashboard.
cloak.copyFail: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.
cloak.lead: Your earnings arrive in your wallet and anyone can see them. Here you move part of them to another address without the explorer showing the link between the two.
cloak.leadNote: It works on the live network (mainnet), separate from the test network used in the rest of Solvers. Sales stay public on purpose: that's what gives buyers confidence. What stays protected is what you do with the money afterwards.
cloak.walletTitle: Your wallet on the live network
cloak.rpcHint: The default read endpoint limits browsers: set NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOAK_RPC_URL.
cloak.emptyTitle: No balance on the live network
cloak.emptyText: To withdraw, send USDC and about 0.005 SOL (for network fees) to the address above, on the live network. Solvers' test USDC isn't valid here.
cloak.destPlaceholder: Paste the address that will receive
cloak.destHint: Use an address just for this: the accountant's report lists the withdrawals that arrived there.

problems.amount_invalid: Enter an amount in USDC, for example 2 or 2.50.
problems.amount_too_large: For safety, private withdrawals are limited to 1,000 USDC at a time while the feature is new.
problems.destination_invalid: That destination address doesn't look valid.
problems.destination_same_as_wallet: Use an address different from your wallet's, otherwise there's nothing to hide.
problems.usdc_insufficient: You don't have that USDC balance on the live network.
problems.sol_insufficient: You're short on SOL (0.005) on the live network for network fees.

cloak.failNote: If the amount was already shielded, it shows up below so you can complete it.
cloak.doneNote: On the explorer, the deposit shows up in your wallet and the withdrawal shows up at the destination (view destination), with nothing linking one to the other.

hides.title: What this hides, and what it doesn't
hides.hidden: Hidden: the link between your wallet and the destination address, and the balance you keep.
hides.from: From whom: competitors, customers and anyone looking at the explorer.
hides.notHidden: Not hidden: your sales and revenue (public on purpose), the fact that you use Cloak, the amount and the time (in a small pool, similar amounts and times can suggest the link) and what Cloak sees: it receives the accountant key when it registers the wallet.
hides.gain: Upside: you choose who sees the history. Give the key to your accountant and they see everything; the public sees nothing.
hides.alpha: Cloak is new (alpha), the code isn't open source and the audit hasn't been published. Start with small amounts.

acct.title: Accountant key
acct.text: It's a read-only key: whoever has it can see the history of your private withdrawals, but can't touch the money. It's rebuilt from your wallet, so you don't need to store it.
acct.afterFirst: The report becomes available after your first withdrawal.
acct.reading: Reading the history (takes a few minutes)…
acct.retrying: {missing, plural, one {# transaction is} other {# transactions are}} missing; reading again ({attempt}/{attempts})…
acct.partial: File generated, but {missing, plural, one {# transaction} other {# transactions}} didn't show up (the network refused some reads). Try again in a moment.
acct.ready: Done: {count, plural, one {# transaction} other {# transactions}} in the file.
